Subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks again for taking the time today, Jordan — great conversation. Per our discovery, here’s a short recap and the next steps we discussed related to PII, retention, and residency for the Acme customer workflows that will call the Redwood API.

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: customer support automation — prompts will include end-user PII (name, email, ticket text).
- Constraint: data residency requirement for EU and US regional isolation for different product lines.
- Procurement asks: explicit statement of what is stored, how long, and whether Redwood uses prompts/outputs for training.

What Redwood confirmed on the call (high-level) — we will follow up with formal documentation:
- Hosted API (default): prompts and outputs are logged for 30 days for debugging, billing, and quality monitoring.
- No training: Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs to train models unless there is an explicit opt-in agreement.
- Dedicated/Private: options available where logs are not retained by Redwood (customer-managed), and data remains in customer-managed VPC or on-prem.

Next steps
1) I’m looping Neha (security) and Marissa (solutions) to provide a short written confirmation covering: exact retention windows, redaction/opt-out controls, residency options, and a short data flow diagram (attached).
2) We’ll provide a 1-page attestation you can share with procurement/legal and a slot for a technical deep-dive next week (Marissa).

Attachments: redwood-pii-data-flow.pdf, redwood-security-faq_v3.pdf

If you can confirm which of your workflows will definitely include PII (and which region they should be pinned to), we’ll tailor the attestation for procurement.

Best,

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise, procurement-friendly confirmation you can include in the Acme SOW/PO. Happy to expand or sign an attestation on company letterhead if that helps.

Short answers (procurement-friendly)
- What is stored: by default, Redwood Hosted API stores request payloads (prompts) and model outputs for the purposes of billing, troubleshooting, abuse monitoring, and quality improvement. That includes the raw prompt text and the generated response.
- Retention window: default retention is 30 days. After 30 days, logs are automatically deleted from active logging systems. For archived debugging snapshots (rare, investigatory use), logs may be retained longer but only with explicit internal approvals and customer notification.
- Training opt-in: Redwood does NOT use customer prompts/outputs to train or improve pre-trained models unless there is an explicit opt-in agreement documented in writing.
- Flagged content/security investigations: In cases where we need to investigate potential abuse or security incidents, related logs may be retained until the investigation concludes. This is exception-based and logged in our internal audit trail; customers are notified if their data is included in such an investigation.
- Data residency: When you pin workloads to a region (e.g., eu-west-1), customer data (prompts/outputs) remains within that region for processing and storage. For hosted accounts, metadata required for global billing/operational monitoring is minimized and pseudonymized; no raw EU-region PII is moved to the US for processing. If your compliance needs require stricter guarantees, our Dedicated/Private offerings ensure no Redwood-managed copies of logs are retained outside your environment.
- Opt-out / redaction controls: Customers can opt-out of logging at the account/org level or send prompts with client-side redaction. We also provide a request header flag (do_not_log=true) that prevents storage of that request's payload/output (subject to SLO tradeoffs).
- Encryption & access: All data is encrypted in transit and at rest. Customer-managed KMS keys are supported for Dedicated/Private deployments. Access to logs is audited; role-based access controls limit who in Redwood can view production logs.

Attachments included: redwood-pii-data-flow.pdf (diagram), redwood-security-faq_v3.pdf (full FAQ and SOC2 pointer).

If you’d like, I can: 
- Draft a one-page attestation for procurement with these bullets on company letterhead (we can sign).
- Set up a short technical call with Marissa (solutions engineer) to walk through the EU residency proof, KMS setup, and the opt-out header behavior.

Let me know which you prefer and any specific wording procurement wants in the SOW.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Applied Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Jordan — thanks. Quick confirmation and next steps from my side: 

1) Explicit sentence for SOW (you can paste this): "Redwood Inference will not use customer prompts or generated outputs to train or improve models without an explicit, documented, and signed opt-in agreement with the customer."

2) do_not_log header operational note: setting do_not_log=true prevents Redwood from persisting that request’s payload and output to standard logging stores (used for debugging and quality). Billing events are still recorded (we bill on API usage); rate limiting and latency SLAs remain as-is, but Redwood cannot troubleshoot that specific request if you have problems because the payload is not retained.

3) Investigations: Redwood will notify the named Acme contacts if we need to retain logs past the standard retention window for an investigation and will provide copies of retained items on request (subject to legal process where applicable).
